module-3-sales-leaderboard-project.label: Module 3 Premium Product Leaderboard
module-3-sales-leaderboard-project.summary: Build one ranked premium-product report, add a scarcity tie-breaker, then trim it to the top five rows.

mp-1-rank-by-price.title: Rank premium products by price
mp-1-rank-by-price.prompt: The sales team is preparing a premium-product review. Return `name` and `price` from `products`, in that order, with the highest price first.
mp-1-rank-by-price.hint: Arrange larger price values before smaller ones.

help.concept: The primary sort defines the main ranking.
help.hint_1: Add the ranking after the products source.
help.hint_2: The largest price should appear first.

mp-1-rank-by-price.solutionCode:
SELECT
  name,
  price
FROM products
ORDER BY price DESC;

sourceChecks.message: Use the `products` table in the FROM clause.
Select the required columns in the requested order: `name`, `price`.

mp-2-add-stock-tiebreaker.title: Add a low-stock tie-breaker
mp-2-add-stock-tiebreaker.prompt: Operations wants lower-stock items to appear first when two products share the same price. Add `stock` to the result. Keep highest price as the primary ranking, then use lower stock as the tie-breaker.
mp-2-add-stock-tiebreaker.hint: Keep the approved price ranking and add stock as the second sort key.

help.concept: A secondary sort changes order only inside rows tied on the primary sort.
help.hint_1: Higher prices must still appear before lower prices.
help.hint_2: For equal prices, lower stock values should appear first.

mp-2-add-stock-tiebreaker.starterCode:
SELECT
  name,
  price
FROM products
ORDER BY price DESC;
mp-2-add-stock-tiebreaker.solutionCode:
SELECT
  name,
  price,
  stock
FROM products
ORDER BY price DESC, stock ASC;

sourceChecks.message: Use the `products` table in the FROM clause.

mp-3-finish-leaderboard.title: Publish the top-five list
mp-3-finish-leaderboard.prompt: The campaign has room for five products. Keep the approved price and stock ranking, then return only the first `5` rows.
mp-3-finish-leaderboard.hint: Preserve the complete ranking, then apply a final row-count limit of five.

help.concept: LIMIT keeps the first rows of an already ranked result.
help.hint_1: Do not change the two sort expressions.
help.hint_2: The completed ranked result should contain only the first five rows.

mp-3-finish-leaderboard.starterCode:
SELECT
  name,
  price,
  stock
FROM products
ORDER BY price DESC, stock ASC;
mp-3-finish-leaderboard.solutionCode:
SELECT
  name,
  price,
  stock
FROM products
ORDER BY price DESC, stock ASC
LIMIT 5;

sourceChecks.message: Use the `products` table in the FROM clause.

sketch_project_brief.title: Project brief
sketch_project_brief.bodyMarkdown:
The sales team is choosing premium products for a limited campaign.

Start by ranking every product from highest price to lowest. Operations then wants a consistent tie-breaker: when products share the same price, show the lower-stock item first so scarcity is visible. Finally, the campaign can feature only five products.

Build one leaderboard and carry the approved query forward at each milestone instead of starting over.
